description: The rating's ratio is the average of the per-film rental-price-to-replacement-cost ratios.

b.request: For each film rating, display the average per-film rental-rate-to-replacement-cost ratio, the number of films in that rating, and the difference between that rating's average ratio and the overall average ratio across all ratings.
b.sql: SELECT f.rating, AVG(f.rental_rate / f.replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS num_films, AVG(f.rental_rate / f.replacement_cost) - (SELECT AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film) AS difference FROM film f GROUP BY f.rating ORDER BY f.rating
b.raw: For each film rating, display the average per-film rental-rate-to-replacement-cost ratio, the number of films in that rating, and the difference between that rating's average ratio and the overall average ratio across all ratings.

d.request: For each film rating, calculate the mean of the per-film (rental_rate / replacement_cost) ratios, then show the rating, that mean ratio, the film count, and the deviation of that rating's mean from the overall mean of all five ratings' means.
d.sql: WITH film_ratios AS (SELECT rating, rental_rate / replacement_cost AS ratio FROM film), rating_stats AS (SELECT rating, AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film_ratios GROUP BY rating), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(mean_ratio) AS overall_avg FROM rating_stats) SELECT rs.rating, rs.mean_ratio, rs.film_count, rs.mean_ratio - om.overall_avg AS deviation FROM rating_stats rs CROSS JOIN overall_mean om ORDER BY rs.rating

c.request: For each film rating, what is the ratio of rental price to replacement cost? Show the rating, that ratio, the number of films, and how far the ratio is above or below the plain average of the ratios across all ratings (the rating's ratio minus that average). Averages ignore missing values. Don't round. The rating's ratio is the average of the per-film rental-price-to-replacement-cost ratios.
c.sql: WITH rating_stats AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS rating_ratio, COUNT(*) AS num_films FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(rating_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM rating_stats) SELECT r.rating, r.rating_ratio, r.num_films, r.rating_ratio - o.avg_ratio AS difference_from_average FROM rating_stats r CROSS JOIN overall_avg o ORDER BY r.rating

a.request: For each film rating, first divide each film's `rental_rate` by its `replacement_cost`, then average those per-film ratios within the rating (averages ignore missing values). Show the rating, that average of per-film ratios, the number of films, and that value minus the plain average of the five rating-level values. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH film_ratios AS (SELECT rating, rental_rate / replacement_cost AS ratio FROM film), rating_averages AS (SELECT rating, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film_ratios GROUP BY rating), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_avg FROM rating_averages) SELECT ra.rating, ra.avg_ratio, ra.film_count, ra.avg_ratio - oa.overall_avg AS difference FROM rating_averages ra CROSS JOIN overall_average oa
